sourceSpec.title: Frontend-independent Rust Bridge for Windows and macOS
sourceSpec.description: Fresh Rust application engine and replaceable web frontend in a thin Tauri shell. UI iteration is a primary product goal: all first-release flows must run against deterministic typed mocks without game/native/backend dependencies. Windows x64 and Apple Silicon macOS are independently planned and qualified. Intel Mac host support is outside this release; actual game process architecture on Apple Silicon still governs injected payload pairing. Existing behavior and test scenarios inform requirements; C#/WPF implementation preservation is not a constraint. Canonical Profiles and producer ownership remain separate.
acceptanceCriteria: Rust engine and domain have no Tauri/webview dependencies; CLI and UI use one command/event contract.
Mock browser development supports all player journeys and failure/progress/draft/recovery states without native dependencies.
One visible install/profile selection with captured operation targets; ordinary and isolated requests remain distinct.
Windows x64 and Apple Silicon macOS have actual build, runtime, package and accessibility evidence.
Shared Profiles retains native catalog/storage/game update/exclusion ownership; no second catalog/updater.
Mod management, schema-driven settings/Data Sync, launch, game management, diagnostics and independent Bridge update are usable.
Plans/revisions/physical identities revalidated under retained exclusions; losing writers have no durable side effects.
Cancellation/disconnect/restart and fault recovery are honest and idempotent.
Three trust domains and per-platform artifact pairing/signing are independently verified.
Frontend semantic/accessibility/visual tests and actual WebView2/WKWebView UX qualification are required.
Dependency work is executed by explicit repo-scoped packets with real commands and receipts.
No placeholder gates, inferred account identity, reused WPF qualification or one-OS release substitution.
sourceSpec.technicalContext: Proposed frontend default: Svelte + TypeScript + Vite; Tauri is a replaceable shell adapter. Rust crates: bridge-contracts/domain/engine/profiles/toml/platform-windows/platform-macos/cli/updater. Canonical repositories remain existing checkouts. macOS Profiles registration, ordinary setup, coordinated launch/loading, update and browser/Keychain qualification are open prerequisites. Installed LexRunner2.1.0 supports FeatureSpecv0, ExecutionPlanv1, plan schema validation and Kahn dependency ordering. Rich work packages bind owners/scopes/gate requirements; Runner scheduling projection is planning-only until exact issues/heads/native hosts/gates are materialized.
sourceSpec.constraints: Planning only. No product code, branch switches, worktrees, runs, attempts, merges, builds, deployments or game cycles. ALLOW_MUTATIONS and automatic Lex frame emission remain disabled. Shared databasePath must be explicit for future coordination. Every owner uses canonical cwd and scoped continuity; Mac roots/host bindings must be resolved on real Mac before execution. Current branches are observations, not designated implementation branches. Root integrates; at most three active implementation workers plus root.

subIssues.title: Product scope, ownership and operating contract
subIssues.description: Owner Bridge; lane integration. Supersede Windows/WPF ownership for the new Bridge; do not relocate existing mac launcher or mod runtime. Ratify first-release journeys, architecture matrix, frontend default and native dependency responsibilities. Record proposed in-process engine hosting and safe normal-exit versus forced-termination recovery rules. Map existing behavior/test scenarios into requirements without preserving C# implementation. Create the fail-closed qualification dispatcher and gate inventory; record unavailable host/script/receipt as blocked, never success. Gate state: planned/not implemented. Detailed owner/write scope/native host/gates are in work-packages.json.
acceptanceCriteria: Required host matrix is Windows x64 and Apple Silicon macOS; shell/game/native module architectures are matched explicitly. Intel Mac host qualification is excluded by user direction.

acceptanceCriteria: Contradictory targets, unsupported version and malformed/unknown commands fail explicitly.
Requests and events carry request/operation IDs; snapshots carry revision and events monotonic sequence.
Commit idempotency keys bind exact input; replay after response loss returns original operation/status, while conflicting reuse rejects.
Prepare tokens bind target/revisions/artifact/schema identity and expire across restart; they do not grant permission or locks.

subIssues.title: Operation ownership, journal and recovery kernel
subIssues.description: Owner Bridge; lane engine. Headless Rust command dispatcher, prepared-plan registry, resource admission, durable operation/journal state and event stream. Deterministic fake ports for contention, cancellation, crash/restart and idempotent recovery. Choose and record process custody: first release hosts the engine within each CLI/Tauri process; safe shutdown retains admitted work until completion, while abrupt process death requires durable recovery. A daemon is a separate later design decision. Gate state: planned/not implemented. Detailed owner/write scope/native host/gates are in work-packages.json.
acceptanceCriteria: Losing writer returns busy before downloads/staging/backups/journals; one exact mutation owner.
Commit revalidates physical/revision identities while retaining owning exclusions.
Webview/CLI disconnect cannot release the writing worker lease; cancellation is requested/cancelled-before-commit/too-late/committed/recovery-required.
Normal host close during native work defers process exit until safe durable state; forced process kill leaves restart recovery, never a claim that work continued after death.
Commit replay after response loss resolves original operation without a second mutation; conflicting input with the same idempotency key rejects.
Uncommitted plans invalidate on restart; admitted durable work remains inspectable by operation ID.
Fault injection at every durable boundary yields committed, rolled-back or explicit recovery-required state.
